reasoning: March 2025 set a record low of 14.1 million km² for Arctic sea ice extent. Evidence shows early 2026 Arctic ice at ~13.2 million km² (Feb), suggesting potential for a new record low in March 2026. However, one source reports ice thickness at Cape Chelyuskin reached 145 cm in late Feb 2026—the highest in 6 years—suggesting some recovery. The Arctic experienced its warmest year on record (Oct 2024-Sept 2025) and continues warming >2x global rate, supporting continued decline. Conflicting signals: thin multi-year ice and record low volumes favor a new low, but recent thickness gains and one contrarian source claiming slowdown since 2005 introduce uncertainty. Given the strong downward trend, record warmth, and early 2026 data suggesting ice below 2025 levels, a new record low is more likely than not, but not certain.
